title: Knowledge Assessment
intro: Test your understanding with multiple-choice, true-or-false and practical questions, review key ideas with flashcards, and finish with a final assessment. Questions focus on reasoning and application, not only memory. Every answer has an explanation.
objectives: Check your understanding of every chapter.
Apply concepts to realistic workshop situations.
Identify the chapters you should review.
summary: Aim for at least 70% on the final assessment.
Review the chapters linked to any questions you missed.

mcq.q: A driver doubles highway speed. What happens to the energy the brakes must remove?
mcq.e: Motion energy rises with the square of speed, so doubling speed means about four times the energy.

mcq.q: Why can hydraulic brakes send force to all four wheels so effectively?
o: The pedal is a long lever
mcq.e: Because the fluid is practically incompressible, pressure applied at the master cylinder is transmitted to every wheel brake.

mcq.q: Which part of a drum brake pushes the shoes outward?
mcq.e: The wheel cylinder pistons push the shoes outward against the drum.

mcq.q: A vehicle's pedal slowly sinks to the floor when held under steady pressure, with no visible leak at the wheels. What is the most likely area to investigate first?
mcq.e: A sinking pedal suggests internal leakage in the master cylinder or an external leak. A leak into the booster may not be visible at the wheels.

mcq.q: Why does the master cylinder have two hydraulic circuits?
o: So a failure in one circuit does not remove all braking
mcq.e: A split system keeps some braking available if one circuit fails.

mcq.q: What does the brake booster do?
mcq.e: The booster multiplies pedal force, usually using engine vacuum or an electric pump.

mcq.q: Inner and outer pads on one caliper show very different wear. What should you suspect?
mcq.e: Uneven wear between inner and outer pads commonly points to sticking slide pins or a piston that is not moving freely.

mcq.q: Where should the minimum pad thickness come from?
mcq.e: Service limits vary by vehicle and must come from the manufacturer's information.

mcq.q: What should be used to support a vehicle that has been raised with a floor jack?
mcq.e: Jacks lift; jack stands support. Never rely on a jack alone.

mcq.q: Why should compressed air not be used to blow brake dust off parts?
o: It cools the parts too fast
It puts hazardous dust into the air
mcq.e: Brake dust should be treated as hazardous and must not be put into the air for people to breathe.

mcq.q: A spongy pedal that firms up after pumping most likely indicates...
o: Air in the hydraulic system or worn/out-of-adjustment brakes
mcq.e: Air compresses, so the first stroke feels soft. Pumping reduces the travel and the pedal firms up.

mcq.q: Which of these is a typical result of brake fluid absorbing moisture?
o: Lower heat resistance of the fluid and corrosion risk
mcq.e: Moisture-laden fluid is less resistant to heat and encourages corrosion inside the system.

mcq.q: What does the amber ABS warning light usually mean?
o: ABS has a fault and may not function, though normal braking usually remains
mcq.e: An ABS fault disables the anti-lock function. The base brakes usually still work, but the fault needs diagnosis.

mcq.q: During an emergency stop in an ABS vehicle, the pedal pulses. What should the driver do?
o: Keep firm pressure on the pedal
mcq.e: Pulsing is normal ABS action. Hold firm pressure and steer.

mcq.q: Which system is most likely to retain heat because its parts are enclosed?
mcq.e: Drum brakes enclose the friction parts, so heat escapes more slowly than from an exposed disc.

mcq.q: A learner finds fluid inside a rear drum and wet shoes. What is the most likely cause?
mcq.e: Wheel cylinder seals leak into the drum. The contaminated shoes must be replaced.

mcq.q: Why should a torque wrench not be used to loosen fasteners?
mcq.e: Using it for loosening can upset its calibration, making later torque readings inaccurate.

mcq.q: Which tool measures rotor runout?
mcq.e: A dial indicator measures small movement, such as rotor face runout.

mcq.q: A vehicle pulls to one side when braking. Which is the best first step?
o: Check tire pressures and compare the brakes on both sides
mcq.e: Logical diagnosis starts with simple checks and comparison of sides before replacing parts.

mcq.q: What is the correct way to deal with a confirmed brake fluid leak?
o: Top up the fluid and continue driving
Do not drive, find and repair the source
Ignore it if the level is above MIN
mcq.e: A leak is a safety defect. It must be traced and repaired before the vehicle is driven.

mcq.q: Why should friction material never be touched by lubricants?
o: It reduces friction and braking ability
mcq.e: Lubricant on friction surfaces reduces friction and can cause brake failure.

mcq.q: Brake pads and shoes should be replaced...
mcq.e: Replacing in sets keeps braking even across the axle and prevents pulling.

mcq.q: A hard brake pedal with the engine running most likely suggests...
mcq.e: A hard pedal commonly indicates loss of power assist from the booster or its vacuum supply.

mcq.q: Which statement about brake fluid is correct?
o: Use the type specified by the manufacturer
mcq.e: Different fluids can be incompatible. Always use the specified type from a sealed container.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of a brake adjuster in a drum brake?
o: To keep the shoe-to-drum clearance correct as the lining wears
mcq.e: The adjuster takes up clearance so pedal travel stays correct as the linings wear.

mcq.q: A new set of pads squeals immediately. Which check is most appropriate?
o: Check hardware, shims, lubrication of specified contact points and installation
mcq.e: Noise often relates to hardware, contact points or installation, so inspect these first.

mcq.q: Why might a vehicle with an electric parking brake need a service mode?
o: To retract the rear actuators safely for rear brake work
mcq.e: The actuator must be retracted using the manufacturer's procedure before the rear brakes are serviced.

mcq.q: When measuring a rotor, why take several readings around the disc?
o: To detect uneven wear or thickness variation
mcq.e: Thickness variation can cause pulsation, and it only shows up when measuring at multiple points.

mcq.q: Which action best protects the environment when changing brake fluid?
o: Pour the old fluid down a drain
Collect it in a sealed labelled container for approved disposal
Leave it on the ground to dry
Mix it with engine oil in the sump
mcq.e: Brake fluid must be collected and disposed of through approved channels.

mcq.q: Which is the best description of brake maintenance work in this guide?
o: A replacement for the service manual
General education that must be supported by vehicle-specific data and supervision
mcq.e: The guide teaches general principles. Specific specifications and procedures come from the manufacturer, and practice needs supervision.

tf.q: The parking brake always uses the same hydraulic circuit as the service brakes.
tf.e: Most parking brakes are mechanical (cable) or electric and work independently of the hydraulic circuit.

tf.q: A small brake fluid leak can be ignored if the reservoir level is above MIN.
tf.e: Any leak is a defect and can lead to loss of braking.

tf.q: Disc brakes generally shed heat better than drum brakes.
tf.e: The disc is exposed to the air, which helps cooling.

tf.q: It is acceptable to estimate torque values if the manual is not available.
tf.e: Torque must be taken from the service manual. Never guess.

tf.q: Brake dust should be blown off with compressed air to keep the workshop clean.
tf.e: This puts hazardous dust in the air.

tf.q: ABS can make a vehicle stop in a shorter distance on every surface.
tf.e: ABS helps steering control and often shortens stopping distance, but not on every surface, and it cannot add grip.

tf.q: A floor jack is a safe replacement for jack stands.
tf.e: Jacks can fail or slip. Always support the vehicle on stands.

tf.q: Brake fluid can damage painted surfaces.
tf.e: Most brake fluids damage paint, so spills must be wiped away quickly.

tf.q: Worn pads can cause damage to the rotors if they are not replaced in time.
tf.e: Worn-through pads cause metal-to-metal contact and score the rotor.

tf.q: Replacing the pads on only one wheel of an axle is good practice.
tf.e: Pads should be replaced in axle sets to keep braking even.

tf.q: A soft pedal can be caused by air in the hydraulic system.
tf.e: Air compresses, so pedal travel increases and feels soft.

tf.q: Brake lubricant may be applied to the pad friction surface to stop noise.
tf.e: Lubricant must never touch friction surfaces.

tf.q: The red brake warning light staying on while driving should be treated as a serious fault.
tf.e: It may indicate low fluid or a hydraulic fault. Stop safely and have it inspected.

tf.q: Resurfacing a rotor is allowed even if it would go below the minimum thickness.
tf.e: A rotor below minimum thickness must be replaced.

tf.q: A mechanical parking brake needs periodic inspection for cable stretch and seizure.
tf.e: Cables stretch and corrode, causing poor holding or sticking.

practical.q: A customer says their brake pedal feels lower than before. Describe the first three checks you would do and why.
practical.a: Check fluid level and condition (low level suggests a leak or worn pads), check the pedal feel while pressing and holding (sinking suggests a leak, spongy suggests air), and inspect pads, shoes and brake adjustment for wear. These steps are quick and find the most common causes before parts are replaced.

practical.q: Explain the correct sequence for raising a vehicle to remove a wheel.
practical.a: Park on level, firm ground; set parking brake and transmission; chock the wheels that stay on the ground; loosen wheel nuts slightly; place the jack at the lift point; raise; place jack stands at the support points; lower onto stands; shake-test; then remove the wheel.

practical.q: How would you check whether a brake caliper is sticking without removing it?
practical.a: Compare the wheel temperature left and right after a short drive, taking care as parts can be hot. Check pad wear differences between inner and outer pads and left and right. With the wheel raised and supported, turn it by hand to feel for drag, and check the slide pins and boot condition.

practical.q: Why is it wrong to top up brake fluid and ignore the cause when the level is low?
practical.a: A low level indicates either worn friction material or a leak. A leak can cause loss of braking, and ignoring the cause leaves a safety risk. The cause needs to be found and repaired.

practical.q: Describe how you would document a brake inspection.
practical.a: Record date, vehicle details, mileage and complaint; each measurement with its units and the specification used; parts replaced; fluid used; torque values and their source; road test result; recommendations; and sign-off.

practical.q: What precautions would you take when cleaning brake parts?
practical.a: Wear PPE, never blow dust with compressed air, use an enclosed brake washer, dust vacuum or approved wet method, keep cleaner away from heat sources, avoid cleaner on rubber parts if the manufacturer warns against it, let parts dry, and dispose of waste properly.

practical.q: A vehicle vibrates through the pedal when braking from high speed. List possible causes and how you would test them.
practical.a: Possible causes include rotor thickness variation or runout, an out-of-round drum, loose or unevenly tightened wheel nuts, or suspension wear. Test with a dial indicator for runout, a micrometer for thickness at multiple points, check wheel nut torque, and inspect suspension.

practical.q: Why must the reservoir level be watched during bleeding?
practical.a: If it runs low, air can be pulled into the master cylinder and lines, which defeats the purpose of bleeding and may require starting again.

practical.q: How do you decide whether a worn rotor can be resurfaced?
practical.a: Measure thickness and compare to the minimum marked on the rotor or in the manual. Resurfacing is only allowed if the thickness after machining stays above the minimum. Otherwise replace it, usually in axle pairs.

practical.q: Explain why pulling to one side under braking should not be solved by simply replacing pads.
practical.a: The cause may be a sticking caliper, collapsed hose, contaminated friction material, uneven tire pressure or suspension fault. New pads will not fix those, and a hidden fault may damage the new pads.

practical.q: What should be checked after replacing brake pads, before the vehicle is driven?
practical.a: Fasteners torqued to specification, wheel nuts torqued in sequence, no leaks, fluid level correct, pedal pumped firm, wheels turn freely, parking brake works, warning lights normal.

practical.q: How would you explain to a beginner why a drum brake is more difficult to inspect than a disc brake?
practical.a: The drum covers the shoes, springs, adjuster and wheel cylinder, so the drum must be removed to see them. A disc brake's pads and rotor are partly visible through the wheel.

practical.q: What is the difference between a general educational procedure and a vehicle-specific repair instruction?
practical.a: A general procedure explains principles and steps. A vehicle-specific instruction contains the exact specifications, torque values, limits, sequence and special tools for that vehicle, and comes from the manufacturer.

practical.q: Describe what you would do if you discovered a damaged brake hose on a vehicle that is due to be driven away.
practical.a: Tell the supervisor and the owner. Do not release the vehicle until the hose is replaced, then bleed the system and complete the final inspection.

practical.q: How can the pedal feel help you narrow down a fault? Give three examples.
practical.a: Soft or spongy suggests air or moisture; sinking suggests a leak or master cylinder failure; hard suggests booster or vacuum fault; pulsing suggests rotor or drum variation. Each points to a different area of the system.
